explanation: After her death, many of her statues and images were smashed or chiselled away, probably on the orders of her successor, Thutmose III. Her terraced temple at Deir el-Bahari still stands.

claims.text: Hatshepsut ruled Egypt as pharaoh in the 1400s BC, roughly from 1479 to 1458 BC.
Hatshepsut was often depicted with the ceremonial false beard of a pharaoh.
Nefertiti and Nefertari were royal wives of the 1300s and 1200s BC, and Cleopatra ruled in the 1st century BC, so none ruled as pharaoh in the 1400s BC.
Many statues and images of Hatshepsut were destroyed after her death, probably on the orders of Thutmose III.
Hatshepsut's mortuary temple at Deir el-Bahari still stands.
